liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): This song features a good jam and a somewhat incomplete bidness section; The reviewer highlights Bill Kreutzman's performance specifically on this song [4][13]
- **Cold Rain And Snow** (1 review): The reviewer states they always liked this particular song from the set [5]
- **Hard To Handle** (1 review): The climax of this number occurs around the seven and a half minute mark [4]
- **Loser** (1 review): The listener notes that this track features two distinct guitar solos [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **I Second That Emotion**: rare: 7 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd71-04-18.sbd.fink.7112.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 17 songs; 123 min; rated 4.44/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: The reviewer notes that Bill Kreutzman is in the pocket and sounds great; Phil's bass is described as electric, delivering a jive to the upstate New York crowd; Recording quality is found superior to most spring 1971 recordings, with prominent Phil bass [6][7][15]
- **gd1971-04-18.sbd.lai.6251.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 123 min; rated 4.12/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: The reviewer prefers the sound of the Grateful Dead from 1971 over later years; Pigpen's magic is described as always a treat, noting he was the music [12]
- **gd1971-04-18.sbd.130710.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 121 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [3]

## Around the show

- The band reportedly received new Macintosh amps from the factory for their upstate New York shows [6]
- The reviewer describes Cortland as a pitstop for Van Halen and Metallica in the 80s [7]
- Bobby compared the field house to a Space Craft Assembly Building in his banter [8]
- The listener used to get high and bike around listening to this tape repeatedly [10]
- The reviewer describes the venue as tiny while praising the show quality [11]
- Banter includes Bobby telling the electrician not to mess with the lights again [15]
- Reviewers found it unnoteworthy compared to the incredible Princeton University concert the previous night [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-04-18.sbd.fink.7112.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by John Valter and Alan J. Fink; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: The only copy the reviewer holds is a horrible cassette acquired in the early 90s; The file was patched using Cool Edit 96 from a higher generation cassette [1][8]
- **gd1971-04-18.sbd.lai.6251.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Mike Lai; source: SBD>MR>??>DAT>CDR [2]. Also: Seeded to etree by Mike Lai, with thanks to Paul B. for the shows; The song cuts at three minutes and twenty-one seconds [2]
- **gd1971-04-18.sbd.130710.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Recording Info: SBD > MR > C > C > C; Transfer Info: C > Nak DR2 > WAV > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > FLAC; This fresh transfer is a nice upgrade over existing… [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Bob Marks Grateful Dead: [1971-04-18 Lusk Field House, S.U.C.N.Y, Cortland, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1971-04-18-lusk-field-house-s-u-c-n-y-cortland-ny-usa/) [17]
- Poster by Wook.FM: [I Second That Emotion | Grateful Dead | Wook.FM](https://wook.fm/grateful-dead/song/i-second-that-emotion) [18]
- Poster by Grateful Dead of the Day: [Dead of the Day: April 18, 1971](https://gratefuldeadoftheday.com/04-18-1971/) [19]
